sections.description: Overview of the patient's history leading up to presentation, focusing on respiratory complaints that mimic central hypoventilation.
subtopics: "Chief complaint": recurrent choking during meals and sleep affecting solids and liquids equally
"Timeline": onset shortly after motor vehicle accident ±14 years ago followed by chronic occipital headaches
"Evolution": progression from mild headaches to frequent nocturnal choking nights
"Home pulse‑ox findings": asymptomatic desaturation episodes down to 70–80% recorded during pandemic period
"Key physical exam findings": normal vitals except brief low saturation spikes without dyspnea
"Prior investigations": three flexible laryngoscopies and two upper GI endoscopies reported normal
"Social impact": avoidance behaviors limiting dining outings, contributing anxiety–depression stress

sections.description: Stepwise elimination strategy employed during the initial work‑up resulting in a focus on neurologic causes.
subtopics: "Laryngopharyngeal reflux" ruled out by normal pH probe despite longstanding nausea
"Gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease" excluded clinically via absence response to maximally tolerated acid suppression
"Myasthenia gravis" excluded based on negative acetylcholine receptor/MuSK antibodies AND lack diurnal fatigability
"Primary pulmonary disease" dismissed following chest radiograph/CT + normal pulmonary function tests/PFTs
"Obstructive sleep apnoea" minimally present on type III polysomnography (AHI 6 · 0), mainly central events (>70 %)
"Neurogenic dysphagia" suggested by equal difficulty swallowing solids/liquids without mechanical obstruction
"Brainstem compression" considered when conventional etiologies failed despite progressive inspiratory difficulties

sections.section_title: "Pathophysiology Of Chiari I Malformation And Respiratory Manifestations"
sections.description: Anatomical-conceptual bridge relating cerebellar tonsillar herniation to autonomic breathing disturbances.
subtopics: "Chiari I definition": cerebellar tonsils descending ≥5 mm below the foramen magnum
"Posterior fossa volume mismatch": developmental constriction producing volumetric displacement
"CSF outflow obstruction": compromised aqueductus cerebri mechanics contributing energy inefficiency
"Medullary centre compression": interruption of nucleus tractus solitarius/ventrolateral medulla responsible for automatic respiration
"Voluntary versus automatic breathing anteriorly controlled via cortical pathways", remain functional despite brainstem disturbance
"Lower cranial nerves IX–XII injury": explains dysphagia/choking sensations alongside sensory vertex pain/allodynia
"Acquired ‘Ondine’s curse’" distinction derived from adult compression rather than PHOX2B mutation driven congenital syndrome

sections.description: "Radiological‐based verification", holding serial review data establishing definitive diagnosis.
subtopics: "Re‑reviewed non‑contrast head CT”: crowded foramina magnum + loss CSF space noted retrospectively post–trauma scan
"Sagittal MRI sequence": documented >11 mm tonsillar descent confirming Chiari I malformation
"Syrinx absent”: exclusion limits severity spectrum
"Polysomnography limitations": type III lacks EEG superimposing total recording time inflating AHI(8); true SPT cannot be derived
"Predominant central apnoea component (>72 %)”: aligns perfectly with medullary autonomic centre putative disturbance
